deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no computation. It is a heavily corrected prose draft of the methodological conclusion of Riemann's 1851 doctoral dissertation (Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse). The preceding folio drafts the dissertation's opening of §20 ("Die Einführung der complexen Grössen in die Mathematik hat ihren Ursprung ... in der Theorie einfacher Abhängigkeitsgesetze"). The following folio drafts the integral lemmas: vanishing of the boundary integral around a removable point, and path independence of the integral of X dy/ds - Y dx/ds.

Content of the page, restated:

(1) Purpose. Riemann wants to indicate what his investigation has gained for the theory of these functions, i.e. analytic functions w = f(z) arising from algebraic or Abelian dependencies.

(2) Critique of earlier methods. Earlier methods all started from some explicit expression of the function, a 'Bestimmungsart und Grössenoperationen' (series, products, integrals). To prove that another expression represents the same function, one had to transform the one into the other, i.e. show the two agree for every value of the argument.

(3) What his theory gives. Agreement on a suitably restricted part of the data already suffices: in his theory part of the determining data is a consequence of the rest. The data are thereby reduced to exactly the extent required. The text of this sentence is partly illegible.

(4) Program. A first attempt is struck out. The second version reads: 'It seems more appropriate to the nature of the matter not to start from a particular expression of the function, but to put at the head the determination of the Gestaltung of the function, as our investigation makes possible.' Concretely, the Gestaltung is:
- the domain, i.e. the Riemann surface T spread over the plane;
- the boundary values;
- the discontinuity conditions.
On this the derivation of the general properties is to be based. Only then does one pass to the various expressions the function admits. These are to be regarded essentially as methods for computing its values at particular arguments.

(5) Example (sketched, then partly cancelled). For functions arising from a given kind of 'Grössenoperationen', the character of the function is expressed by limit and discontinuity conditions. 'Wird z.B. das Gebiet ...' breaks off and resumes with '— so erhält man eine algebraische Function.' In modern terms: a function single-valued and meromorphic on a closed (compact) Riemann surface spread over the sphere, with only pole-type singularities, is algebraic in z. This is the principle of Riemann's 1857 theory of Abelian functions; the dissertation §20 states it in just this sketched form.

(6) Closing. He ends this investigation, whose aim is the foundations of a theory of simple dependency laws between variable quantities. He leaves undiscussed the question of the intermediate link between these general foundations and their concrete application.

Nothing implicit needs filling: there are no formulas.
errors: No mathematical steps on the page, so no mathematical errors. The algebraic-function example is only gestured at ('Wird z.B. das Geb. — so erhält man eine algebraische Function'). The hypotheses (closed surface, finitely many poles, single-valuedness) are not stated on this page; they are supplied in the published §20 and in the 1857 Abelian functions paper.

results.what: Methodological principle: define and study an analytic function by its domain (Riemann surface), boundary and discontinuity conditions, not by an analytic expression; expressions serve only as computational methods
results.modern_name: Riemann's geometric/conceptual approach to complex function theory (existence-theoretic definition of functions)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Inaugural dissertation 1851 (§20), elaborated in Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen 1857

results.what: Uniqueness/overdetermination: part of the data of a classical definition follows from the rest, so agreement on a restricted set suffices to identify two expressions
results.modern_name: Identity theorem / uniqueness via Dirichlet principle (data reduced to boundary and singularity conditions)

results.what: A function on a closed Riemann surface over the plane with only polar singularities is an algebraic function
results.modern_name: Meromorphic functions on compact Riemann surfaces are algebraic (Riemann existence theorem context)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known concluding methodological section (§20) of Riemann's 1851 dissertation. The published text says essentially the same thing, so the page adds only drafting variants.

checkable.asserts: Illustration of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions defining Riemann's 'function of a complex variable'. Polynomial expressions satisfy them; nothing on the page itself is computational.

Trivial example of an algebraic function w satisfying w**2 - z = 0, two-valued over the plane and single-valued on its two-sheeted Riemann surface. This is the kind of function the 'algebraische Function' remark refers to.

transcription_corrections: Line 4: '(Darstellungsweise[?] ... Grössenoperationen)' should read '(Bestimmungsart und Grössenoperationen)', matching the phrase on the previous folio.
'hieraus' before the struck word is more likely 'hieran'.
'zu beweisen[?]' is more plausibly 'zu knüpfen'; the reading is uncertain.
Near the end, 'und legen uns die Frage' should be 'und lassen ... die Frage ... unerörtert'.

The sentence beginning 'Durch unsere Untersuchung ist die Möglichkeit ... verificirt[?]' is largely conjectural in the machine transcription. The published §20 analogue says that 'ein Theil der Bestimmungsstücke eine Folge der übrigen ist'. The draft likely expresses the same idea (agreement in a restricted range suffices), but the exact words are uncertain.
